one_liner: Gladly has a broad documented REST API with Basic auth (agent email + API token), a sandbox and webhooks. The pages show no self-serve signup, so credentials come from a customer's Gladly instance.
auth_notes: Token-based Basic auth: username is the agent email and password is an API token. The user needs the API User permission to create tokens. Tokens are tied to one user and one environment (sandbox or production). The Lookup API is signed requests for Gladly calling the customer's service, not third-party client access. No OAuth2 appears in the docs.
access_notes: Tokens are created inside a customer's Gladly instance by an admin-provisioned API user. The pages show no free tier or self-serve signup, and the homepage only offers a demo. This is inferred from absence rather than stated, so confidence is low.
blocker_notes: No self-serve path to credentials appears in the pages. Each customer admin must create an API user and token, so setup is per customer. A sandbox is enabled by Gladly. No MCP server evidence appears in the pages, and the draft's community MCP URL was dropped as unsupported. The verdict could also be ready_with_friction if a customer account counts as per-customer setup.

evidence.quote: Gladly API uses token-based Basic Authentication
API tokens are tied to a single user account and a particular environment.
For integrations not built by Gladly, a Gladly Administrator should
enable the Gladly API in a separate sandbox environment
Resources follow REST semantics and utilize industry-standard HTTP verbs, response codes, and authentication schemes.
Create up to 50 webhooks for your organization.
